questions.stemHtml: The given image of the cell wall belongs to which of the following organisms ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Neisseria meningitidis
  • Presence of lipooligosaccharide, pilus and capsule confirm the organism to be Neisseria.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker’s textbook of microbiology, 10th Edition, Page No 234-236

questions.stem: Which of the following has the least risk of perinatal transmission?
questions.solutionHtml:
Rubella
  • Rubella has the least risk of perinatal transmission


NELSON TEXTBOOK OF PEDIATRICS 21ST EDITION PAGE NO. 1678

questions.stem: A Pregnant woman comes for an antenatal check-up. She has a history of stillbirth at 28 weeks in her previous pregnancy. She also has a history of multiple sexual partners and vaguely remembers having a painless ulcer on her vulva prior to her last pregnancy. What would be the first step of investigation for this lady?
questions.solutionHtml:
VDRL test
  • History of painless vulvar ulcer in her last pregnancy and stillbirth at 28 weeks, with a history of multiple sexual partners is suggestive of Syphilis. The first step should be to do a confirmatory investigation which is VDRL


ANANTHANARAYAN AND PANIKER’S TEXTBOOK OF MICROBIOLOGY 9TH EDITION, PAGE NO. 75

questions.stem: A CSF sample of an elderly male presenting with meningitis is subjected to gram staining and revealed gram-positive bacilli. Which of the following is true regarding the motility of the causative agent?

options.label: A
options.text: Motile at 25 Degree Celsius and immotile at 37 degree Celsius

options.label: B
options.text: Motile at 37 Degree Celsius and immotile at 25 degree Celsius

questions.answerText: Motile at 25 Degree Celsius and immotile at 37 degree Celsius
questions.solutionHtml:
Motile at 25 Degree Celsius and immotile at 37 degree Celsius
  • History of meningitis in an elderly male with a gram positive bacteria in CSF is more likely to be Listeria monocytogenes. Listeria monocytogenes is motile at room temperature(20-25 degree celsius) but not at 37 degree celsius.


ANANTHANARAYAN AND PANIKER’S TEXTBOOK OF MICROBIOLOGY 10TH EDITION PAGE NO. 402-403

questions.stem: Which of the following is a protozoan parasite that can be seen inside Kupffer cells?
questions.solutionHtml:
Leishmania donovanosis
  • Leishmania donovani is a species of intracellular parasites belonging to the genus Leishmania, a group of haemoflagellate kinetoplastids that cause the disease leishmaniasis.


PANIKER’S TEXTBOOK OF MEDICAL PARASITOLOGY 8TH EDITION, PAGE NO. 13,14,32

questions.stem: A lady cleans her cat litter regularly to avoid infection by toxoplasma during her pregnancy. What is the infective stage of these organisms in the cat feces?
questions.solutionHtml:
oocyst
  • The cat,specifically the definitive host, is responsible for the sexual reproduction of Toxoplasma gondii. Inside the cat’s intestines, the parasite produces oocysts.
  • These oocysts are then shed in cat’s feces. After being shed in the environment,the oocysts require a period of time, usually 1 to 5 days to undergo sporulation. Sporulation makes the oocysts infective.


https//www.cdc.gov/parasites/toxoplasmosis/epi.html

questions.stem: An elderly male patient who underwent a kidney transplant 10 years back is on immunosuppressive therapy. He gives a history of cough and dyspnea for the past 1 week, and the sputum microscopy shows gram- positive budding yeasts cells and pseudohyphae. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Invasive candidiasis
  • Invasive candidiasis occurs when Candida yeast gets into your bloodstream and spreads to internal organs.


Rook's Textbook of Dermatology, 9th edition, Chapter 32 Fungal Infection

questions.stem: Protein misfolding is associated with disease called?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prion disease
  • Prion diseases are transmissible, untreatable, and fatal brain diseases of mammals. Their cause is highly unusual: The host's normal prion protein can, for unknown reasons, malfunction and assemble into structured aggregates called prions that cause infectious brain disease.


Ananthanarayan and Paniker’s Textbook of Microbiology 10th Edition, Page No. 560
